results.summary_before: The Retro Console is an 8.5-bit game console implemented in Verilog that generates VGA video and audio. It includes a PPU that produces pixels from tile, map, and sprite data, and a synthesizer that mixes four voices at 96 kHz. The design is tested using an RP2040-based RAM emulator that provides program and graphics data, with VGA output via a Pmod and audio output left to external hardware. Silicon tests confirm the graphics work, but the synth portion has not been tested.
results.summary: The Retro Console is an 8.5-bit retro game console implemented in Verilog across a 3x2 tile area. Its PPU generates pixels from tile, map, sprite and palette data and outputs them as VGA, while its synth mixes four voices at 96 kHz. An RP2040-based RAM emulator provides program and graphics data, and VGA output requires a Pmod; audio output is left to the RP2040 and is still to be determined. Silicon tests confirm the graphics work, but the synth portion has not been tested.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi project is a 3-bit asynchronous down counter in which each flip-flop clocks the next, with a button used to advance the count. It is meant to drive a 7-segment display as external hardware. A tester ran it through the Commander application and found that ui_in[0] acts as the clock rather than the real clock, and that the observed output sequence 102, 63, 7, 79, 109, 6, 125, 91 repeats, suggesting the output bits are scrambled relative to the intended display. The silicon behaviour therefore only partially matches the intended counter.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi project lets a user select a number from 1 to 8 with DIP switches and indicates whether it is even or odd using LEDs and a 7-segment display, with logic gates such as AND, OR, XOR, NAND and NOT involved. Switching on 2, 4, 6 or 8 is intended to light all blue LEDs and show 8 on the display. A tester confirmed that the odd/even detection works on silicon but that the 7-segment output does not match the Wokwi simulation because the display is wired differently on the board. The project is a logic-gate teaching exercise and needs an external seven-segment display.
